name: Sandler Selling System
origin: David Sandler, 1967; Sandler (formerly Sandler Training). The 'Sandler Submarine'.
summary: Seven submarine compartments in order: Bonding & Rapport, Up-Front Contracts, Pain, Budget, Decision, Fulfillment, Post-Sell. Equal-footing, low-pressure selling: qualify hard (Pain -> Budget -> Decision) before ever presenting, and inoculate against remorse after the close.
motion: Mid-market consultative and full-cycle sellers; strong qualification discipline.

traits.name: Bonding & Rapport
traits.definition: An equal-footing, low-pressure tone where the buyer speaks freely — no eager-seller behavior.
classifying_questions: Did the rep establish an equal-footing, low-pressure tone (no eager-seller behavior)?
Did they match the buyer's communication style?
Was psychological safety evident — the buyer speaking freely, including about negatives?
miss_signals: buyer gives guarded one-line answers throughout

coaching.why_it_matters: Sandler selling runs on the buyer telling you the truth; truth requires a peer dynamic, not a vendor dynamic.
coaching.next_move: Open the next call with a nurturing, no-pressure frame and one honest disqualifier to signal you're not desperate.
coaching.example_line: It may turn out we're not a fit — I'd rather we find that out together in the next twenty minutes than after a long demo.

traits.name: Up-Front Contracts
traits.definition: An explicit agreement at the start: purpose, time, both agendas, and the possible outcomes — including that 'no' is acceptable. Mini-contracts before transitions (demo, pricing).
classifying_questions: Did the rep set an explicit agenda with time, purpose, and agreed possible outcomes at the start?
Did both sides agree on what happens at the end of the call — including that 'no' is an acceptable outcome?
Were mini-contracts set before transitions (e.g., before demoing or discussing pricing)?
met_signals: 'by the end of this call we'll decide X or Y' stated and agreed
miss_signals: call drifts with no agreed outcome
ends with 'I'll send some info over'

coaching.why_it_matters: Without a contract for the call, you get the mutual mystification Sandler warned about — polite endings and ghosted follow-ups.
coaching.next_move: Script a 30-second up-front contract and deliver it before anything else on the next call.
coaching.example_line: We've got 30 minutes. I'd like to ask about the dialer problems, you'll have questions for me, and at the end let's agree either on a next step or that it's not a fit — fair?

traits.name: Pain (Pain Funnel)
traits.definition: Running the pain funnel — surface -> example -> impact -> personal cost — until the BUYER concludes the pain matters, quantified in money, time, or emotion.
classifying_questions: Did the rep run a pain funnel — surface statement, concrete example, business impact, personal cost?
Did they quantify the pain in money, time, or emotion?
Did the buyer, not the rep, conclude that the pain matters?
met_signals: 'can you give me an example... what has that cost you... how do you feel about that?' progression
buyer says some version of 'we have to fix this'
miss_signals: first pain statement taken at face value
rep supplies the impact narrative themselves

coaching.why_it_matters: People buy emotionally and justify intellectually — the funnel walks the buyer from a fact to a feeling they will pay to change.
coaching.next_move: Take this call's strongest surface pain and go two levels deeper next time: a concrete example, then what it costs them personally.
coaching.example_line: Can you give me a specific example of the last time that happened — and what did that end up costing you?

traits.name: Budget
traits.definition: Openly discussing whether the buyer is willing and able to invest money, time, and resources — BEFORE presenting.
classifying_questions: Did the rep openly discuss whether the buyer is willing and able to invest (money, time, resources)?
Was budget surfaced before any presenting or pricing reveal?
Did they test comfort with the likely price range?
met_signals: a range floated and reacted to
miss_signals: rep hopes the demo will justify the number later

coaching.why_it_matters: Presenting before budget is qualified is free consulting; Sandler qualifies the wallet before the show.
coaching.next_move: Introduce a money bracket in the qualification phase of the next call, matter-of-factly.
coaching.example_line: Teams your size typically invest between X and Y with us — is that in the universe of what you'd spend to fix this?

traits.name: Decision
traits.definition: Mapping the who, how, when, and why of the decision — process, parties, and timeline agreed.
classifying_questions: Did the rep map who, how, and when the decision gets made?
Were all parties involved in the decision uncovered?
Did they get agreement on what the decision timeline looks like?
miss_signals: 'send a proposal and we'll see' accepted

coaching.why_it_matters: A deal you can't map is a deal you can't forecast — surprises in the decision process are always bad ones.
coaching.next_move: Before fulfillment, walk the buyer through 'what happens between yes and signed?' and write the steps down together.
coaching.example_line: Suppose you love what you see — walk me through what happens next on your side, step by step.

traits.name: Fulfillment
traits.definition: Presenting ONLY against the pains qualified earlier — no feature dumping — and asking for a decision at the close, not a 'think it over'.
classifying_questions: Did the presentation address only the pains uncovered earlier (no feature dumping)?
Did the rep confirm the solution closes each qualified pain?
Did they seek a decision at the close of fulfillment rather than accepting 'think it over'?
met_signals: 'does that solve the problem you described?' checks
miss_signals: full product tour regardless of pains
call ends on 'we'll think about it' unchallenged

coaching.why_it_matters: Every feature beyond the qualified pains adds risk and price objections without adding desire.
coaching.next_move: Structure the next demo as a checklist of their three pains; ask for a thumbs-up-or-down after each.
coaching.example_line: You said missed follow-ups were the killer — here's exactly and only how that goes away. Does this close it?

traits.name: Post-Sell
traits.definition: Inoculating against buyer's remorse and competitor pull-back after the yes; locking next steps and onboarding.
classifying_questions: Did the rep inoculate against remorse ('is there anything that could reverse this decision?')?
Did they proactively surface competitor pull-back or internal second-guessing?
Did they lock concrete next steps or onboarding before ending?
met_signals: 'what could derail this between now and signature?' asked
onboarding step scheduled on the call
miss_signals: no rehearsal of the internal pushback the champion will face

coaching.why_it_matters: Deals unravel in the 48 hours after yes, when the incumbent calls back and finance asks 'why now?' — inoculate before you hang up.
coaching.next_move: After the next verbal yes, ask what could reverse it and rehearse the buyer's answer to their toughest internal skeptic.
coaching.example_line: Before we book onboarding — is there anyone or anything that could unwind this decision next week? Let's handle it now.
